production.note: US model years per Classic.com: 'The Aston Martin DB5 was produced for model years 1963 to 1965', 'arrived in 1963 as a successor to the DB4' and 'Built until 1965'. RM Sotheby's: '1,059 units built between 1963 and 1965' (rmsothebys-db5-1964). Sold new in the US: chassis 1796/L was 'Built for the North American market ... retailed by Aston Martin Lagonda Inc and despatched to its first owner, a certain Mr Kupperman of New York City' (jbl-db5-1796). Aston Martin did not use US model years as such; no Aston page states them. The DB5 Vantage (higher-output engine) is not covered by this record's figures.

body.note: Aston Martin lists 'Saloon' (a two-door fixed-head car, a coupe here) and 'Convertible'. The handful of coachbuilt shooting brakes are not included. Convertible availability in the US was not separately confirmed.

displacementL.note: 3,995 cc. Aston Martin: 'DOHC Straight six, 3995 cc'.

fuel.note: Carburetted petrol six; inferred from the description.

drivetrain.note: Front-engined, rear-wheel drive; inferred from the description (live rear axle with lever-arm dampers).

transmission.note: Aston Martin: '5-speed ZF box or optional Borg-Warner 3-speed automatic'. RM Sotheby's: '...fully synchromesh ZF five-speed manual transmission with overdrive' (rmsothebys-db5-1964).

powerHp.note: Aston Martin's rating as published; the standard is not named, treated as SAE gross per the rule for pre-1980 cars (powerStandard Other). Quote (Aston Martin): "DOHC Straight six, 3995 cc, 282 bhp @ 5500 rpm 280 lbs-ft @ 4500 rpm" (reproduced on a second request). Classic.com: 'the DB5 produced 282hp in standard guise, while the more potent Vantage version delivered 325hp' (classic-db5). No separate US rating was found.

weightLb.note: 1,468 kg x 2.20462 = 3,236.4, rounded to 3,236 lb. Quote (Aston Martin specification block): "Weight: 1468kg" (reproduced on a second request). The label is a plain 'Weight' and the body is not stated (probably the Saloon); read as a kerb weight per the guide's rule for unlabelled Aston Martin figures. Step 1 of the weight order. Not a US-specific figure.
